name: Boss Suites Nana
detail: It was about a 10-minute walk from the train station, so the access was good. The receptionist spoke a little Japanese. I was having trouble figuring out how to get the shower water to come out, but when I told the front desk, they came to my room with me and assisted me.

name: Sunday Harbour View Sukhumvit 50 Hotel
detail: Very good. Even though it's no longer part of the Ibis chain, the quality is still there. The room is small, the air conditioning is cool, the bed is good, and the soundproofing is not great but it’s not bad. It's great to find cheap accommodation in the city. The hotel’s location may not be on the main street, and the entrance looks a bit dark, but the hotel has parking. The staff is lovely, the hot water flows strong, and I slept comfortably. It's very worth the price for what you get.

name: Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Bangkok
detail: I'm glad I chose this hotel for my first time in Thailand. The room was lovely and clean, and the view of Terminal 21 and the intersection from the window was beautiful. There were always staff members who could speak Japanese, which gave me peace of mind. I apologize for any inconvenience caused with the laundry, but I appreciate their very kind assistance. I would love to stay here again. Thank you very much! ♪

name: Grand Mercure Bangkok Atrium
detail: The cost-performance ratio is particularly high, the view from the room is very good with large windows, and the room is very quiet at night. The mattress is super soft; I really don't want to get up. There is a small river behind the hotel where it seems you can take a boat. There is also a currency exchange machine next to the hotel, and a 7-Eleven on the right side when you go out, which is very convenient. The hotel staff is especially enthusiastic and the service is very attentive. Next time I come to Bangkok, I will stay here again.

name: ibis Styles Bangkok Sukhumvit Phra Khanong
detail: The cleaning is thorough and very clean! The pool isn't large, but the atmosphere is nice, and we enjoyed it even with kids! The staff were also very accommodating, there was a kids' club, and they provided a baby crib, making it perfect for a family vacation! It's a bit of a walk from the station, but it wasn't a problem when we used Grab to get around! There's also a local market nearby, and it was truly a wonderful stay!

name: Convenient Grand Plus Hotel Suvarnabhumi
detail: I forgot my favorite doll in the hotel room, so I called back to the hotel, and they delivered it to my house. I was very impressed. If I get the chance, I would stay there again; it’s nearby and the price is not high. The room is spacious, there’s an elevator, and a swimming pool. We booked at a price of 480 baht through Agoda, which is considered affordable. The room has twin beds, it’s large, with comfortable cool air conditioning, and a clean bathroom. I slept well without any noise disturbance, the water pressure is strong, and it has hot water, shower caps, a hairdryer, coffee, and a coffee maker. The mattress is soft, and there’s no bad smell in the room, which is okay for this price. It’s also close to Suvarnabhumi Airport, which is very impressive. My mother slept comfortably and was very satisfied because we brought elderly and children along. It’s a great place for anyone looking for accommodation near the food market and not far from Suvarnabhumi Airport; I recommend this place, and the price is reasonable too.

name: The Bless Hotel & Residence
detail: This hotel is conveniently located near Phrom Phong Station. It is just a few minutes' walk to large commercial facilities like EmSphere and Emporium, making it very convenient for shopping. There are many massage shops, restaurants, and places to enjoy at night in the surrounding area, and since it is a place with many Japanese residents, it's reassuring that Japanese can be understood at some places. With BTS Phrom Phong Station nearby, accessing various areas of Bangkok is easy, making it a convenient location for both sightseeing and shopping. Although the building itself shows some age, it is well-maintained. The guest rooms are quite spacious and stylishly decorated. There was also a sofa, which allowed me to relax after returning to the hotel. The bathroom has separate shower and bathtub facilities, and the toilet is equipped with a washlet. The amenities made it comfortable for Japanese guests, as NHK is also available on the television. Considering the current hotel prices in central Bangkok, I think there are not many hotels in this price range that offer this location and room size. I felt that the balance of location, size, and price is very good. The only disappointment was that there was no hot water from the shower during my stay. The cold water shower was very chilly, so I would appreciate it if this could be improved. Besides that, I was very satisfied and can recommend this hotel to those who want a reasonably priced spacious room around Phrom Phong.

name: The Quarter Ladprao by UHG
detail: I was very impressed with the accommodation. The room was clean and tidy, the atmosphere was good and quite quiet, making it suitable for relaxation. The amenities in the room were relatively complete, and the staff provided good service, speaking politely and being very helpful. The location was convenient for travel. Overall, it was worth the price paid. If I have the opportunity to visit this area again, I would want to stay here again. 😊

name: Asia Hotel Bangkok
detail: It was great to be directly connected to the station since it was the rainy season. I could leave my luggage anywhere and go out again. There was no balcony, but the room was spacious, clean, and comfortable. There was a bathtub, which allowed me to enjoy a luxurious time. There wasn't an electric kettle, but there was a hot water server in front of the elevator. I wanted to drink coffee as soon as I woke up, so I brought paper cups and instant coffee with me. The hotel staff was also friendly. I had previously stayed at cheap hotels nearby that cost about 1,000 baht per night, but this time the hotel was about 1,700 baht per night. This quality is worth the price. I plan to stay at this hotel again the next time I go to Bangkok.

name: Furama Silom Hotel Bangkok
detail: To ride BTS, you first need to get to MahaNakhon. However, it's not a big problem in Bangkok because it's easy to use taxis or motorcycles. Also, MahaNakhon is not very far, so you can walk there, and you can see MahaNakhon from the rooftop pool of the hotel. I saw a review mentioning cockroaches, but there were none. However, the lobby and hotel corridors felt a bit scary as the hotel is old. Haha. But the rooms were cleaner than I expected, and the rooms were spacious, which was nice. The air conditioning was great, and the bathroom was large with a decent-sized bathtub, which was good for relieving fatigue. The staff was friendly. I reserved breakfast, but I overslept every day, so I couldn't eat. Haha. The pool isn't very big, but the view is nice, and there’s also a bar with a great view. However, there was not much shade at the pool, so we couldn't stay long. Hahaha. Across the hotel, a pretty nice landmark building is going to be built in Bangkok within a few years. They are working hard on it now. So, I think this hotel will have quite a good location then. Right next to the hotel, there is a 7-11, which was very convenient! The hotel was old and a bit worn out, but the rooms were still comfortable for the price. It’s located in an area where you can enjoy the nightlife, but it's also far enough from that area, so the surroundings of the hotel were quiet, which was nice. In fact, there are many graves in this area. Haha. I always found it cheap on Agoda and debated whether to book it, but it turned out better than expected, making me want to visit again. It seems like one of the few remaining hotels in Silom that offers good value for the price.
